slides.title: The big idea
slides.html:
A parallelogram is a rectangle if and only if its diagonals are equal. A parallelogram is a rhombus if and only if its diagonals are perpendicular, and also if and only if each diagonal bisects a pair of opposite angles.

Proof (rectangle): in rectangle ABCD, triangles ABC and DCB share BC, have AB = DC and right angles at B and C, so they are congruent by SAS, and AC = DB. A square has all of these properties: equal, perpendicular diagonals that bisect each other and its angles.
